speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
text: asked the Minister for Education in respect of the 2024 Secondary 1 posting exercise (a) how many Primary 6 students are not posted to any of their six school choices, with a breakdown into (i) numbers (ii) percentages and (iii) posting group; (b) how does this posting outcome compare to the numbers in the previous three years; and (c) whether any guidance or preparation is given to parents for years where there are more competition for places in secondary schools such as years with higher birth rates.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Education)
text: This means that every student who takes the PSLE and qualifies for secondary school will be guaranteed a place at one of our secondary schools.
The 2024 PSLE cohort was larger than cohorts in the previous years and this was taken into account in our planning.
Schools' cut-off points, or COPs, can fluctuate from year to year, depending on the cohort's PSLE score and their school choices.
When more students with the same PSLE score pick the same schools, the COPs of these schools could become more stringent than what they were in previous years.
The larger cohort taking the PSLE in 2024 could also have contributed to this effect for some of the popular schools.

Therefore, besides encouraging students and their parents to only use the previous year's COPs as a reference, we have strongly encouraged them in 2024 to select at least two or three schools where their PSLE score better than the school's previous year's COP.
This would increase their chances of securing a place in one of the preferred school choices.
We also encourage students and parents to look beyond COPs and to consider the school's culture and distinctive programmes alongside the students' strengths and interests.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The first relates to guidance given to parents over choices as the Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned earlier, because of the larger cohort this year, there were some fluctuations that were experienced in the COPs.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Parents have given us feedback that there were some difficulties in choosing the schools that their children might have been eligible for.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: My question would be, would there be any extra guidance given to parents, given that this is obviously quite a stressful period for them trying to figure out which schools, which choices to make for their children, especially given that this is still a relatively new system that everyone is not quite so familiar with.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, firstly, whether any further guidance is going to be given to parents in terms of choosing.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: On the point about COPs, can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary confirm how many schools actually had reduced COPs compared with the 2023 cohort?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: As the Senior Parliamentary Secretary is aware, every time when the school posting results come out, there are parents who wish to appeal.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: For this year, I would like the Senior Parliamentary Secretary to confirm how many appeals were received in order to try and get their children into the schools of choice that they did not gain a posting for?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: How many appeals were made, how many were successful?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And would the parents be given guidance in the future about, for example, if their children did not get any of the six choices, would they be given additional guidance or prompts whether an appeal is possible and also how to make an appeal?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I understand that there was some confusion among some parents about how to go about appealing and when to expect results.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, I think there was some confusion on the ground from what I understand.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, whether the Ministry could actually provide some guidance and support for parents who find themselves and their children in this situation.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And finally, my third supplementary question relates to affiliation benefits.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: There is some sentiment on the ground that there might be some differences in affiliation benefits and the effect that it has under the current system.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I was just wondering whether the MOE is monitoring that, whether there have been any differences found, whether affiliation benefits actually apply more to this new system compared with the last system, and whether there are any tweaks to the system required in order to find out what effect of the affiliation benefits are.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: I think for the first one with regard to the guidance given to parents and so on, most certainly, awareness and education and outreach is definitely very important.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: And that is why the school has done much of the work on the ground, especially before the release of PSLE results, engaging students, reaching out to the parents.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: And on the day of the results, to make sure that they choose a wider cluster of schools, probably the top three choices would be something that they would desire, but that for the bottom three choices, at least select two or three schools that has a much higher COP, so that they make sure that the clustering is a little more diverse.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: Although it is somewhat a good reference, these fluctuations always occur and are very common.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: A plus or minus one point is common for the majority of the schools.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: But then again, out of an entire range from four points up to 20-plus points, plus or minus one point in difference of the COPs is actually quite normal.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: The appeals do go direct to the schools and for each of those desired schools, the parents and the students as well are encouraged to go to the school and then find out the process.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: There is also an online link where the appeals process is well known.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: If those aspects or avenues actually fail, then parents are encouraged to also approach MOE and we will see how we can better facilitate and see if within the vicinity or closer to the vicinity, what are the available schools.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: On the last query on affiliation benefits, this is not exactly related to the posting, so I suggest the Member to post a more specific question on affiliation at the next Sitting.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The first has to do with what the decision in terms of allocation of schools when there is a tie-breaker.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My understanding is that it is a combination of COPs as well as the rank order that the student indicates.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But earlier on, the Senior Parliamentary Secretary indicated that distance was used as a decision metric in terms of allocation after this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Just to clarify, is distance used also for the purposes of a tie-breaker situation?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My second is, I wonder if the Ministry also considers distance not so much just in terms of geographical distance as the crow flies but rather commute time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This is because we have many residents who inform us that even though a specific school may be located relatively close in terms of geographical distance, it could take in terms of commuting time, close to an hour to get there.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Understandably, they would rather have something that could be further but requires less commute time.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: With regard to the specifics on the tie-breaker, the Member actually has filed a Parliamentary Question, which is Question No 47, which we will address in full.
